q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026. As of today (August 21, 2026), there are approximately 5 days until the announcement.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks about NVIDIA's **forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release** — this is asking for Q3 FY2027 guidance, not Q2 results themselves, given the context.

Based on the research provided:
- Current Wall Street consensus for Q3 FY2027 revenue is **$103.1 billion**
- NVIDIA has a track record of guiding conservatively and then beating: Q1 FY2027 actual was $81.6B vs. guidance midpoint, beating by 4.6%
- The range provided (99.5–115.5B) appears calibrated around this Q3 guidance expectation

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will guide to approximately **$103–105 billion** for Q3 FY2027, likely with the standard ±2% range they've been using. This would be:
- At or slightly above the current consensus, showing sustained demand
- Consistent with continued sequential acceleration from Q2 (~$91B)
- Within the provided forecast range, centered reasonably in the distribution

NVIDIA tends to guide conservatively relative to what they can achieve, but they also provide ranges that limit downside risk. Guiding significantly below consensus would disappoint the market, while guiding significantly above would be unusual given their typically measured approach.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro headwinds**: Unexpected weakness in enterprise spending or AI capex cycles
- **China revenue restrictions tightening**: Further geopolitical constraints on China revenue (currently assumed at zero)
- **Competitive pressures**: Accelerated AMD or other competitor traction reducing NVIDIA's share
- **Demand softness signals**: If Q2 actual results disappoint relative to expectations, Q3 guidance would likely be lower
- **Conservative guidance**: NVIDIA occasionally guides below consensus when uncertain about demand sustainability

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected Q2 results**: If Q2 actual beats guidance significantly (as Q1 did), it could signal stronger demand momentum
- **Accelerating data center demand**: Continued AI infrastructure build-out could drive upward guidance revisions
- **No deterioration in China**: If policy environment stabilizes or they find workarounds, releasing previously constrained revenue
- **Strong forward bookings**: Indication of robust customer demand extends guidance upward
- **Market share gains**: If they're winning deals faster than expected, supporting higher trajectory

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research explicitly provides:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue was **$81.6 billion** (actual), beating guidance midpoint by 4.6%
- NVIDIA's standard guidance range: **±2%** around the midpoint
- Current Q3 FY2027 consensus: **$103.1 billion**
- Q2 guidance midpoint: **$91.0 billion** (±2%, so range ~$89.2–$92.8B)

This shows a consistent pattern of guidance at/slightly below consensus with beats on actual results. For the forward guidance (Q3), I would expect similar positioning — at or slightly above current consensus but with measured confidence.

## Probability distribution reasoning

The range 99.5–115.5B is quite wide. The midpoint of 107.5B is slightly above current consensus (103.1B). The distribution should be:
- Heavily weighted toward 102–105B (consensus area)
- Some probability of slightly higher (105–108B) if demand signals are very strong
- Some left tail risk (100–102B) if they're being cautious
- Minimal probability in the extremes (below 100B or above 110B) given current consensus and typical guidance patterns

The median should be very close to the current consensus of $103.1B, perhaps slightly higher given Q1's beat pattern and the fact that the range midpoint is 107.5B (suggesting forecasters expected some upside).

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The company's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects Q2 revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no data center compute revenue from China [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Wall Street analysts, based on 40 to 42 estimates, have an average Q2 revenue consensus of approximately $91.9 billion to $91.85 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). This places the consensus just under 1% above NVIDIA's midpoint guidance and within the company's projected range, which has a ceiling near $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). For comparison, NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, beating its own guidance midpoint by 4.6% [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).

The crucial element for forecasters will be NVIDIA's **Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance**. Current consensus for Q3 FY2027 revenue is $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). A guide at or above this consensus would indicate continued accelerating demand [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). The Q3 guide will also be scrutinized for any changes to the China revenue assumption [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).
